hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: One command per row and no builds: `python memory_graph/gdlmem.py context <fn>` on each of the 35 zero-mechanism entries' functions. A row whose context returns an accepted parked/capped/improved attempt is a CITATION defect; a row whose context is empty is a PROVENANCE defect. This round's claim that the subset is a citation backlog is refuted by any zero-mechanism row whose context comes back empty -- and one such row would be worth more than the three passes reported here.

hypothesis.statement: ROUND 4 SHOULD STOP SAMPLING THE ZERO-MECHANISM SUBSET AND CLOSE IT INSTEAD, BECAUSE THIS ROUND MEASURED THE REPAIR TO BE MECHANICAL. Rounds 2 and 3 have now drawn four functions from it (sndVoiceUpdateAll, plus these three) and all four have a reachable, accepted, source-exhaustion record that the rule entry simply fails to name. The next custodial pass should run `gdlmem context <fn>` across all 35 zero-mechanism groups in one sweep -- no builds, one call per function -- and split them into CITATION (a record exists; write its id into the entry's `mechanism`) and HOLE (context returns nothing; the rule shipped without source-exhaustion provenance and belongs in front of the Mandatory result policy). Report the two numbers. If the HOLE count is zero the backlog is closable by an edit pass to webfrank.json owned by the WF lane; if it is not, the HOLE list is the wanton-use population and is the more important finding this control can produce. Round 4's draw should then come from whatever the HOLE set turns out to be, not from a fresh random sample of a subset already characterised.
